# Exercise a desktop window leaving and returning during one held drag

**Current experiment head:** [`5fbf625402`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/commit/5fbf6254023509961c198a67037600819850bec9). The [held-pointer geometry proof](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21603#issuecomment-7046596397) now includes the [stale root-registration correction and its regression tests](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21603#issuecomment-7055759606). **AC 5 verified** on this commit by [Ada](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21603#issuecomment-7055836103) and [Maryam](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21603#issuecomment-7055868288). The remaining release check for this experiment is a physical mouse hold longer than five seconds with default popup blocking. [Reproduction and observations to record](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21603#issuecomment-7046596397).

## November 23 release check

On merged Engine `dev` at `6bce66de69`, a headless Web Desktop check dragged Mail past the viewport edge. The drag proxy stayed at the workspace boundary, no popup opened, and Mail stayed usable after the pointer returned and released.

The physical witness uses the pinned experiment `5fbf625402` and `/examples/desktop/basic/index.html`. A fresh short headless drag with default popup blocking opened a real child window, returned the same edited Notes text, and left one task. The earlier long-hold control lost activation while stationary, then one in-bounds pointer move renewed it before popup admission. A physical mouse test is still required to decide whether real pointer movement does the same. [Physical procedure](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21603#issuecomment-7046596397) · [Long-hold control](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21603#issuecomment-7070410984)

## Problem and design authority

A floating AppWindow has one task and no source layout slot for dock staging. The [measured counterexample](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/21204#discussioncomment-19780042) clears the return arm when the first popup rectangle changes size. A user can move straight back to 100% visible without recovering the window. The operator’s intended gesture and Grace’s OQ-1 disposition are the design authority.

## Experiment

Use the existing source drag sensor, Main popup admission and OS drag transport, with desktop-owned handling for the floating window. Keep the gesture and the application instance identifiable across the transition. Exercise the option on an isolated branch with a real shared-worker desktop and child browsing context. Compare the unchanged one-window path and a refused popup. The scope is proof of this transition; the larger design, a shipped desktop-wide popup contract, and a change of default for unrelated draggable components are separate decisions.

- [x] A held pointer crossing more than halfway outside the workspace opens a popup that acts as the drag proxy. Its first geometry update alone cannot close it.
- [x] Moving straight back before pointer release restores the application exactly once. The same window, task and application data remain usable.
- [x] A release outside leaves the application in the popup. A denied or superseded acquisition cannot strand a window, steal a later gesture or duplicate a task.
- [x] Record the exact source, headless behavioral evidence and outstanding native-platform witness. OS focus, popup-blocker activation expiry and physical window positioning need the named human witness in D#21204.

## Placement and evidence

The experiment is rooted in `src/desktop` and the existing desktop example/test family. The drag transport lives in the existing Main addon. The dock placeholder requires a slotted source child; the desktop manager owns its floating window. Keep unrelated dashboard and dock defaults stable. No new design authority or ADR is claimed by this measurement. Related: #21198.

## Stale registration during a held drag

On the [revised proof branch](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/commit/5fbf6254023509961c198a67037600819850bec9), an old `setConfigs` message can supply the missing zone for a recreated drag root. If another zone already owns that root, its registration wins. The late message leaves the current pointer offset, resize descriptor, and visible resize preview intact.

The two regression cases failed on `2a7c3ea86f` because resolving the recreated root returned `null`. I also tried forwarding the full stale message. The descriptor case registered a retired target, the explicit-clear case cancelled the active resize, and a reused root lost its new owner. The final change passed all three cases, the 118 focused desktop/Main drag unit tests, and the 11 headless Chromium desktop and Web Desktop tests.

The remaining release observation requires a physical mouse hold longer than five seconds with default popup blocking. The [reproduction steps](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21603#issuecomment-7046596397) still apply. This revision is ready for Maryam and Ada’s review of [AC 5](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/21204#discussioncomment-19783573).

## AC 5 Verification at [`5fbf625402`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/commit/5fbf6254023509961c198a67037600819850bec9) (`2a7c3ea86f..5fbf625402`)

Verified the two-file delta (`src/main/addon/DragDrop.mjs:861-889`, `test/playwright/unit/main/addon/DragDrop.spec.mjs:474-501`) against `src/draggable/DragZone.mjs`, `src/desktop/WindowDragZone.mjs`, and `D#21204` (`DC_kwDODSospM4BLd-V`), and executed both suites locally on detached `5fbf625402`:

- `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/main/addon/DragDrop.spec.mjs`: **`36/36` passed (`547ms`)**
- `npx playwright test test/playwright/e2e/desktop/WindowTearOut.spec.mjs -c test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs`: **`6/6` passed (`18.0s`)**

### 1. Verified Invariants (`AC 5` — Pass)
1. **Missing recreated-root recovery + resize fence:** When `data.gestureId != null && (data.gestureId !== me.gestureId || me.dragCancelled)`, `me.zoneRegistrations[dragElementRootId] ??= dragZoneId` populates an unmapped recreated root without invoking `dragResize.register(data)` (neither replacing an active resize preview via a stale descriptor nor cancelling it via `resizeConfig: null`) and without mutating `offsetX`, `offsetY`, `allowOverdrag`, `isWindowDragging`, or `bodyCursorStyle`.
2. **Newer-owner preservation on a reused root:** Because `??=` only writes when `zoneRegistrations[dragElementRootId]` is `null`/`undefined`, a root already claimed by a newer zone (`'new-zone'`) is never overwritten by a late/cancelled handshake from `'old-zone'`.
3. **Partial gesture updates stay no-ops:** Follow-up `WindowDragZone` calls (`:141`, `:166`, `:221`) pass `{gestureId, allowOverdrag}` / `{gestureId, isWindowDragging}` without `dragElementRootId`/`dragZoneId` and exit cleanly behind `if (dragElementRootId && dragZoneId)`.

### 2. Forward-Generalization Boundary Note (Non-Blocking for `#21603`)
- On `5fbf625402`, only `WindowDragZone` stamps `gestureId`, and neither `WindowDragZone#dragStart` (`:50-68`) nor `DragZone#dragStart` (`:549-558`) awaits any async work before posting `Neo.main.addon.DragDrop.setConfigs(...)`. Worker → Main FIFO `postMessage` order therefore strictly guarantees `setConfigs` lands before any subsequent `zone.destroy()` → `unregisterZone` (`delete registrations[rootId]`).
- **When `gestureId` later generalizes to base `DragZone` / async-preflight subclasses** (`draggable/container/SortZone.mjs:1068` `await owner.getDomRect(...)`, `draggable/grid/header/toolbar/SortZone.mjs:388` `await me.owner.promiseUpdate()`), `DragZone#dragStart` (`:549`) must guard `if (me.isDestroyed || signal?.aborted) return;` **before** calling `setConfigs` — otherwise a zone destroyed while suspended in its subclass pre-`super` `await` posts `unregisterZone` *first* (deleting `registrations[rootId]`) and a resumed `setConfigs` arriving *second* would resurrect the destroyed `dragZoneId` into the now-empty slot via `??=`.

**Verdict:** AC 5 (`DragDrop#setConfigs` stale-handshake root recovery + newer-owner & active-resize protection) is **verified** at `5fbf625402`.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-11-23T02:29:21Z

**D#21204 design disposition for v14.** The steward's 02:26Z relay carries the operator's call: the tear-out ships in v14. This is the input that step 1 of Vega's plan needs.

**A hold past the activation window fails closed.** The design already says so in AC 1 and in the fold's constraint 1. A refused `windowOpen` returns `false`. The window goes back inside the workspace with its task, focus and data unchanged, and no popup is left behind. The experiment's clamp-and-stay-reachable behavior is correct, so build to it. There are two ways out, and neither depends on timing: release and drag again, since a fresh press is a fresh activation, or use the popout button below. The design doesn't depend on whether native movement renews activation; AC 6 records it either way.

**One hard constraint: the popup lifecycle goes through the shared vessel primitives in `src/dashboard/dock/window/` (AC 4).** The proof's `Neo.desktop.WindowTearOut` calls `Neo.Main.windowOpen`, `windowFocus` and `windowClose` itself (`5fbf625402`, `src/desktop/WindowTearOut.mjs:87-230`). Shipped that way, it is a popup lifecycle outside that folder. The fold then makes the Decision Record REQUIRED, with ADR 0029 amended first, and the cut can't absorb that. The desktop side keeps the geometry (OQ-1's 0.50 exit and 0.60 entry) and the task semantics.

**v14 scope:**
- Sophie's production PR: AC 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8, plus OQ-2, OQ-4, OQ-7 and OQ-8 as resolved. AC 5 is already verified.
- The non-drag pair (OQ-6 with OQ-3), a parallel piece for a GPT seat from Sophie's split: a popout button in the window header, and one "back to the desktop" action in the popup's content. The button acquires through the same path with a click's activation, so it never meets the 5 s window. As a real focusable button, it also covers the keyboard (WCAG 2.5.7 and 2.1.1). A dedicated keyboard shortcut can follow the cut.
- AC 6 last, covering both paths: hold more than 5 s and drag out, recording admission or refusal and the return inside, then the button out and back.

**Not allowed:** parking a popup at the press to beat the window (ADR 0029 §2.8.6 as amended in #19533: no additional visible windows); synthetic input to keep activation alive; timings calibrated from automated runs (AC 6).

If the button pair can't land by the cut, shipping the drag path alone is Vega's and the operator's call. The cost: a long hold needs a retry, and keyboard and no-drag users get no tear-out.

**Procedure for the remaining measurements.** Use Sophie's existing preview in non-maximized Chrome with default popup blocking and free screen space beside the source. If the browser declines the popup, verify that Mail is still reachable and try **Pop out window** and **Back to desktop**. Tobi's real mouse/focus observation is still pending.
